quis: quī, quae, quod — who (rel., dat./abl. pl., old form = quibus); also quis, who? (interrog.) · also indefinite quis, anyone (after nē/neu, m. nom. sg.); quis locus, which place? (interrog. adj.) · also indef. after sī, anyone (m. nom. sg.: sī quis) · also indef. after quam (m. nom. sg.: quam quis, until anyone) · also indef. after rel. quae (m. nom. sg.: quae quis, whatever any man)
quisquam: quisquam, quicquam — anyone, anything (in questions and negatives) (nom. sg.)
quo: quī, quae, quod — who, which, what (rel. or interrog., m./n. abl. sg.); quō (adv.), where to · also indef. after nē, any (abl. sg.: nē quō nūmine) · also quō, to what end? why? (quō molem … statuēre?) · also quō (conj.), in order that (quō … averteret)
quod: quī, quae, quod — which (rel., n. nom./acc. sg.); quod (conj.), because, that · also interrog. adj., what? (n. nom./acc. sg.: quod genus) · also acc. of respect, wherefore (quod tē per superōs … ōrō) · also indef. adj. after sī, any (n. nom. sg.: sī quod nūmen) · also connective, but, now (quod sī, 'but if'; n. acc. sg. as conj.)
quos: quī, quae, quod — who, which (rel. or interrog., m. acc. pl.) · quis after sī — any(one) (indef., m. acc. pl.: sī quos)
refert: referō, referre, rettulī, relātum — to bring back; to reply, utter (3rd sg. pres.)
regia: rēgius, -a, -um — royal, queenly (f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.) · also rēgia, -ae (f.), palace, royal house (nom. sg.: rēgia Pīcī)
regio: regiō, regiōnis (f.) — region, district, land (nom. sg.)
rerum: rēs, reī (f.) — thing, matter; pl. circumstances, fortunes (gen. pl.)
rerumque: rēs, reī (f.) — thing, matter; pl. affairs, fortunes, power (gen. pl.) + -que 'and'
res: rēs, reī (f.) — thing, matter, affair; state (nom. sg.; nom./acc. pl.)
ruat: ruō, -ere, ruī, rutum — to rush, fall headlong, collapse (3rd sg. pres. subj.)
rumpere: rumpō, -ere, rūpī, ruptum — to break, break through (pres. inf.)
rutulos: Rutulī, -ōrum (m. pl.) — the Rutulians, Turnus's people in Latium (acc. pl.)
sanguine: sanguis, sanguinis (m.) — blood; descent, lineage (abl. sg.)
se: suī (reflexive pron.) — himself, herself, itself, themselves (acc.; also abl. sē)
secuti: sequor, sequī, secūtus sum — to follow (perf. part. of deponent, m. nom. pl.)
sedem: sēdēs, -is (f.) — seat, abode, dwelling place, site (acc. sg.)
sequatur: sequor, sequī, secūtus sum — to follow, pursue, attend (3rd sg. pres. subj.)
sequi: sequor, sequī, secūtus sum — to follow, pursue (pres. inf., deponent)
sera: sērus, -a, -um — late, tardy (f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.) · also f. abl. sg. (sera nocte)
simoenta: Simoīs, -entis (m.) — Simois, a river of Troy (Greek acc. sg., Simoenta)
sin: sin (conj.) — but if, if on the other hand
sine: sine (prep. + abl.) — without · also sinō, -ere, sīvī, situm, to allow, let (sg. imper.: sine palmula)
sines: sinō, -ere, sīvī, situm — to allow, permit, let (2nd sg. fut.; sinēs)
sinite: sinō, -ere, sīvī, situm — to allow, let (pl. imper.)
sit: sum, esse, fuī — to be (3rd sg. pres. subj.)
solum: solum, -ī (n.) — ground, soil, land (acc./nom. sg.); also sōlus, alone (n. acc. sg.) · also n. nom. sg. (sōlus, alone: hoc sōlum nōmen) · also adv., only, merely
solvere: solvō, -ere, solvī, solūtum — to loosen, free, release (pres. inf.) · also 3rd pl. perf. = solvērunt (agmina … solvēre)
spartam: Sparta, -ae (f.) — Sparta, city of Menelaus and Helen (acc. sg.)
suasit: suādeō, -ēre, suāsī, suāsum — to advise, urge, recommend (3rd sg. perf.)
subducere: subdūcō, -ere, -duxī, -ductum — to draw up from below, haul ashore (pres. inf.)
subegit: subigō, -ere, -ēgī, -āctum — to subdue, force, compel (3rd sg. perf.)
sumus: sum, esse, fuī — to be (1st pl. pres.)
sunt: sum, esse, fuī — to be; there are; sunt mihi, I have (3rd pl. pres.)
super: super (adv. and prep.) — above, over; besides, in addition · also remaining, left over (sōla mei super imāgō) · also prep. + abl., about, concerning (quam super adventū; multa super nātā)
superesse: supersum, -esse, -fuī — to be left over, remain, survive (pres. inf.)
superi: superus, -a, -um — above, upper; superī (m. pl.), the gods above (gen. sg. m.; nom. pl. m.) · also m. voc. pl. (Superī, address to the gods)
superis: superus, -a, -um — upper, above; superī (m. pl.), the gods above (m./f./n. abl./dat. pl.)
surgit: surgō, -ere, surrēxī, surrēctum — to rise, arise (3rd sg. pres.)
tantumque: tantus, -a, -um — so great, such (n. nom. sg., tantum nefas) + -que, and
tegunt: tegō, -ere, tēxī, tēctum — to cover, hide, conceal (3rd pl. pres.)
tela: tēlum, -ī (n.) — missile, weapon, spear, dart (acc./nom. pl.)
tempus: tempus, -oris (n.) — time, season, hour (nom. sg.) · also n. acc. sg. (tempus inane peto)
terra: terra, -ae (f.) — land, earth, ground (nom./abl. sg.) · also f. voc. sg. (ō terra hospita)
terrae: terra, -ae (f.) — earth, land, country (gen./dat. sg.; nom. pl.)
teucri: Teucer, Teucrī (m.) — Teucer, early king of Troy (gen. sg.) · also Teucrī, -ōrum (m. pl.) Trojans (voc. pl.: Teucrī, secludite) · also m. nom. pl. (Teucrī, Trojans)
tibi: tū, tuī — you (sg.); tibi, to/for you (dat.)
totidem: totidem (indecl. adj.) — just as many, the same number
troas: Trōs, Trōis (m.) — a Trojan (acc. pl., Greek form Trōas)
troes: Trōs, Trōis (m.) — a Trojan (nom. pl., Greek form Trōes)
troia: Trōius, -a, -um — Trojan, of Troy (f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.) · Trōia, -ae (f.) — Troy (abl. sg., from Troy) · also nom. sg., Troy (servātaque serves Trōia fidem)
troiae: Trōia, -ae (f.) — Troy (gen. sg.) · also dat. sg., for Troy (sīc fāta ferēbant)
troianos: Trōiānus, -a, -um — Trojan, of Troy (m. acc. pl.)
tua: tuus, -a, -um — your, yours (sg. poss.) (f. nom. sg.) · also n. acc. pl. (tua nūmina) · also f. abl. sg. (tua laude)
tuis: tuus, -a, -um — your, yours (sg. poss.) (m./n. abl./dat. pl.) · also f. abl./dat. pl. (tuīs querēlīs)
tum: tum (adv.) — then, at that time; next
tumidusque: tumidus, -a, -um — swollen, puffed up, proud (m. nom. sg.) + -que, and
turnum: Turnus, -ī (m.) — Turnus, king of the Rutulians, rival of Aeneas for Lavinia (acc. sg.)
tydides: Tȳdīdēs, -ae (m.) — son of Tydeus, Diomedes (nom. sg., Greek patronymic)
tyriis: Tyrius, -a, -um — Tyrian, of Tyre (m./f./n. abl./dat. pl.)
tyrrhenamque: Tyrrhēnus, -a, -um — Etruscan, Tyrrhenian (f. acc. sg., with manum) + -que, and
urbes: urbs, urbis (f.) — city (nom. pl.; also acc. pl.)
ut: ut (conj.) — + subj. so that, in order that; + indic. as, when, how
venus: Venus, Veneris (f.) — Venus, goddess of love, mother of Aeneas (nom. sg.)
versa: vertō, -ere, vertī, versum — to turn, reverse (perf. pass. part., f. abl. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)
vertere: vertō, -ere, vertī, versum — to turn, change, drive (pres. inf.)
vim: vīs (f.; acc. vim, abl. vī) — force, power, violence (acc. sg.)
vincere: vincō, -ere, vīcī, victum — to conquer, win, prevail (pres. inf.)
vobis: tū, tuī — you; vōs, vōbīs, to/for you, by you (dat./abl. pl.)
vocat: vocō, -āre — to call, name, summon (3rd sg. pres.)
xanthum: Xanthus, -ī (m.) — Xanthus, river of Troy (acc. sg.)
